correctness.rationale: For d>=1 the line-intensity polynomial has degree <=2d and its two leading coefficients are independent of height. Thus 2d+1 first-line observations give the whole first trace, forcing equality of the two top coefficients, and 2d-1 second-line observations give the second trace. The rational quotient of two nonzero candidate polynomials is unimodular on both whole lines. Rational reflection identities force a nonzero imaginary period; only constant rational functions have periods, and the constant is unimodular. The zero case is handled by polynomial root counting. This proof covers arbitrary distinct nodes and lower-degree inputs. A 390-trial standard-library exact-arithmetic checker validates interpolation identities but is not used as an infinite/universal proof.

value.rationale: A fixed degree-d complex polynomial has d+1 complex coefficients but loses phase; arbitrary repeated line measurements alone cannot distinguish conjugate-reflected roots. Two separated parallel lines make exact recovery possible with 4d nonadaptive arbitrary-node intensity values, instead of the (2d+1)^2 radial/angular measurements in a direct earlier polynomial construction. The key mechanism is a two-coefficient redundancy between line traces, and the same interpolation map is exactly dimension-saturating on its natural 4d-dimensional ambient polynomial pair space. This is a geometrically natural full family of designs, not an unmotivated finite slice; nonlinear minimality and stability are explicitly unproved.
